A brilliantly addictive, cartoonish sandbox that turns the stress of survival into pure, unadulterated fun.

The original Crashlands is an absolute masterclass in how to make a crafting-survival game that is light on frustration and impossibly heavy on fun. You play as Flux Dabes, an intergalactic galactic delivery trucker who gets stranded on the alien planet Woanope after a floating head named Hewodokoos blows up your ship. From the second your escape pod hits the dirt, the game hooks you with its vibrant, cartoonish art style and a gameplay loop that is the definition of a "time-sink." It takes all the tedious elements of the survival genre—like inventory management and losing your gear upon death—and completely throws them out the window, giving you an infinite pockets system that lets you focus entirely on exploring, smashing things, and building a massive base.

The combat and progression systems are simple to look at but incredibly satisfying to execute. Combat plays out like a high-speed dance; enemies project their attack ranges on the ground in bright red shapes, forcing you to dodge, weave, and strike back with a massive arsenal of craftable weapons and gadgets. The loop of hunting down alien fauna like Wompits and Glutterflies to harvest their bits, using those bits to craft a shinier suit of armor, and then using that armor to hunt down an even bigger monster is utterly intoxicating. When you combine that with a pet system that lets you hatch and raise your own stable of alien monsters, it becomes a game where you sit down to play for twenty minutes and suddenly realize the sun is coming up.

What truly elevates Crashlands into a cult classic, however, is its incredible heart and razor-sharp wit. The dialogue between Flux and her sarcastic robotic companion, Juicebox, is genuinely hilarious, filled with the signature slapstick and "dubstep silliness" that the developers at Butterscotch Shenanigans are famous for. The questing system is massive, guiding you across three completely distinct and massive biomes while introducing a quirky cast of alien races who desperately need your help building everything from living rooms to high-tech weapons. It is the perfect, "no-brainer" game to throw on while listening to a podcast or relaxing after a long day. It’s witty, it's deep, and it remains one of the finest time-wasting adventures on Steam.

[h1] 7 / 10 [/h1]
[h2] 无厘头APRG元素异星生存日记 [/h2]
小时候在手机上通关，最早得知这款游戏是知道开发者三兄弟虽身患癌症但依旧坚持完成的故事。作为一款融合了ARPG的剧情驱动向类饥荒游戏，体验下来就能发现独属于崩溃大陆的特殊魅力。
[h2] 异星宝可梦与角色构筑 [/h2]
宠物系统是游戏的点睛之笔，几乎每一种怪物都可以通过击杀获取其宠物蛋，孵化后宠物不仅能在战斗中助你一臂之力，还会提供各种被动加成，我个人很喜欢收集各种宠物第一次玩的时候把所有能抓都都抓了并且超进化hhhh。随着主线任务的推进，角色装备和武器道具也会随之逐渐升级，成就感慢慢。
[h2] 建造机制和内容设计 [/h2]
本作可惜之处在于建造的驱动性不强，可能性也不高，房子搞个方形反而效率最高，装饰品物品的设计显得有些多余。可能是限于平面的原因，但饥荒证明了明明是可以更好。主线通关后的重玩性也不高，固定的剧情，同样的角色，还不支持多人联机，多少有些意犹未尽。
[h2] 打击病魔的异星情书 [/h2]
开发者虽患病但依旧保持着对游戏的爱与执着，游戏里诙谐幽默的桥段象征着他抗击病魔的乐观心态，玩家很难不被感染，在此祝贺作者现已摆脱病魔。[b] 本作是很值得体验的生存建造宠物收集游戏，当动作生存宝可梦玩乐趣无穷。 [/b]

Finished the full story on Ludicrous difficulty, unlocked all story achievements, and ended with an endgame megabase after ~68 hours.

I actually played this game years ago on my phone using a pirated/modded version when I was still in high school. At the time, my English wasn’t great, so I didn’t fully understand the humor or dialogue. Funny enough, this game ended up motivating me to learn English better, which later helped with my studies and exams.
So yeah..sorry for pirating back then. I bought it properly now, and I’ll definitely be buying Crashlands 2. I’ve been looking forward to it even before I had my own hard-earned PC.

As for the game itself: it’s simple, straightforward, and full of humor that definitely doesn’t belong to this timeline. Tons of references. It’s colorful, easy to understand, and I’d honestly say it’s a good game for kids too. Combat is very readable (just dodge, literally), and who knows..it might even help someone learn to read or pick up a bit of English like it did for me.

Base building isn’t required to finish the game, but if you enjoy designing spaces, it becomes its own endgame. I spent a few “unnecessary” hours just making things look right, and honestly, that was part of the fun. It’s a complete game,not deep, but charming in its own way. This was also my first survival-crafting game, so it has a special place for me.

Of course, it’s not perfect. Combat gets repetitive after a while, and the humor won’t be for everyone. If you want pure action with minimal crafting, this probably isn’t for you..unless you jump straight into Hardcore mode. I didn’t. I’m not that hardcore of a gamer, and I’m mostly excited for Crashlands 2, especially since I’ve heard the base building is improved.

Overall, this is a finished, honest game you can play anytime, however you want.
